7-recommendation-default-on-all-multi-op.remediation_hint: In Phase 7 step 2, broaden the recommendation logic: when the narrow Recommendation gate's four preconditions do NOT all fire, still mark one option as `(recommended)` based on a softer heuristic — (1) smallest blast-radius option that resolves the surfaced item; (2) tie-break by alignment with this PR's stated intent (e.g. fix-now on tightly-scoped feature PRs); (3) further tie-break by the option chosen most often for this surfaced-item type in past runs (read from run_history.runs[].notes). 7-fix-now-default-for-branch-introduced-.description: Phase 7 surfaced an item meeting the 4 original narrow-gate preconditions (LOC <=15, code/docs only, smoke <=60s, canonical small-fix category) AND git blame shows at least one cited file:line is in origin/<BASE_BRANCH>...HEAD BUT the option block landed `(recommended)` on `File as gap` or `Skip with logged justification` instead of `Fix it now`.
7-fix-now-default-for-branch-introduced-.remediation_hint: In Phase 7 step 2, add the 5th narrow-gate precondition (`item was introduced by THIS branch`) verified via `git blame -L <line>,<line> -- <file>` for each cited file:line. When all 5 fire, default-recommend Fix it now with rationale 'branch-introduced + cheap fix; closing before merge is cheaper than filing a follow-up'. In the softer-heuristic fallback, also bias toward Fix it now when any cited file:line is in the current branch's diff (same git blame check, used as tie-breaker ahead of historical frequency). Common cause when this trips: narrow-gate fires on the 4 original preconditions but the recommendation ranking still defaults to File-as-gap because the 5th precondition isn't being checked.
7-fix-now-default-for-branch-introduced-.applied_via: Added 5th precondition (branch-introduced via git blame) to Phase 7 narrow Recommendation gate. Added branch-introduced bias to softer-heuristic fallback ahead of historical-frequency tie-breaker. Per 2026-05-22 suggestions.md convergence proposal (phase7-recommendation-misranks-fix-now-when-branch-introduced).

7-fix-now-applied-without-failing-state-.description: A Phase 7 `Fix it now` flow applied a tightening edit (per the tightening-fix detector in Phase 7 step 2a) WITHOUT recording the pre-edit verification sequence in the audit row evidence.
7-fix-now-applied-without-failing-state-.remediation_hint: In Phase 7 step 2a, before applying any user-approved tightening edit, run the failing-state test/probe and compare the actual observable value to the user's proposed precise value. If they disagree, surface the discrepancy back to the user with three options (adjust precise value to actual / investigate underlying code / skip and file as gap) instead of applying-then-reverting. Record `Pre-edit verification: actual=<X>, expected=<Y>, match=<y|n>` in the Phase 7 audit row evidence so the audit can detect skipped verifications. Common cause when this trips: detector matched a tightening pattern (!= -> ==, range collapse, whitelist narrowing) but the apply step ran without the verification subroutine, repeating the edit+revert ceremony.
7-fix-now-applied-without-failing-state-.applied_via: Added Phase 7 step 2a (Pre-edit verification for tightening fixes only). Includes tightening-fix detector table (operator strictness, membership collapse, range tightening, whitelist narrowing, pattern strictness) and a verification sequence that runs the failing-state test BEFORE applying the edit. Per 2026-05-22 suggestions.md convergence proposal (skill-applied-fix-without-pre-edit-verification).

5-closure-narrative-falsifiable-claims-n.description: Phase 5 accepted a closure narrative paragraph in TRACKER_FILES diff (or COMPLETED_STREAMS.md) containing falsifiable claims (e.g. 'N tests pass', 'no regressions', 'tier X clean') without reconciling those claims against this run's Phase 3/4 actual evidence. Load-bearing because silently accepting a false claim is exactly the failure mode the skill exists to catch.
5-closure-narrative-falsifiable-claims-n.remediation_hint: In Phase 5 step 4c, for each closure-narrative paragraph added in TRACKER_FILES diff (and in COMPLETED_STREAMS.md when present), parse for falsifiable phrases using regex candidates `\b\d{2,5}\s+(unit|integration|smoke)?\s*tests?\s+pass`, `\bno regressions?\b`, `\bsmoke (?:tier\s+)?clean\b`, `\ball tests pass\b`, `\bN/?A failures?\b`. For each matched claim, reconcile against Phase 4 actual results — if Phase 4 has not run the corresponding tier in this session and the claim mentions a tier, surface to Phase 7 as an unresolved item demanding either (a) re-run the tier or (b) explicit user acceptance of the claim. If Phase 4 results contradict the claim, surface the discrepancy to Phase 7 as a hard item (load-bearing FAIL). Cheaper fallback: emit a Phase 5 sub-report row that quotes each claim verbatim alongside the Phase 4 actual result and routes any narrative claim to Phase 7 for explicit user reconciliation.
